full_judgment: 2. Appellant-Pre-emptor is the owner of Plot No.2575 of Mouza Alipur. Some portion of Plots Nos. 2574 and 2573 were transferred by their owner under a kabala dated 3 June 1976, whereupon the appellant filed an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act before the Munsif, Faridpur, claiming pre-emption of both the plots taking the ground that these two plots are contiguous to his own land. His claim was resisted by the respondent-transferee taking the ground that only a part of Plot No. 2574 is contiguous to the appellant's land that Plot No. 2573 is not at all contiguous, and as such he is not entitled to pre-empt both the plots. The trial Court allowed the pre-emption in respect of both the plots finding them to be contiguous to the pre-emptor's land. This finding was confirmed in appeal by the Subordinate Judge. But in revision, as stated above, a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division reversed the finding in respect of Plot No. 2573 and modified the decision of the courts below and allowed pre-emption only in respect of Plot No. 2574 which he found to be contiguous to the pre-emptor's land in Plot No. 2575. The pre-emptor came before us for leave to appeal and leave was granted to consider whether both the Plots, 2574 and 2573, being allegedly contiguous to each other and forming a compact block, should have been allowed on pre-emption on the ground of "contiguity."
